title: Statistics - Conceptual Understanding and Data Transformation
topic: Statistics - Cumulative Frequency, Spread, and Data Effects
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: A cumulative frequency curve is very steep around the median. What does this indicate about the data?
options: Data is widely spread around the median
Data is tightly clustered around the median
questions.explanation: A steep gradient on a cumulative frequency curve means a small range of values contains many data points, indicating tight clustering (small IQR) (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: Two cumulative frequency curves intersect at the 50% cumulative frequency line. What does this imply?
questions.explanation: The 50% cumulative frequency corresponds to the median. If curves intersect there, both data sets have the same median value (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: A data set has mean = 40, SD = 6. If every value is multiplied by 3, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Multiplying all values by k multiplies the standard deviation by |k|. New SD = 3 × 6 = 18 (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: Which measure of spread is most resistant to extreme outliers?
questions.explanation: The IQR uses only the middle 50% of data (Q1 to Q3), so extreme values at the ends do not affect it. Range and SD are sensitive (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: A box-and-whisker plot has a much longer right whisker than left whisker. What does this suggest?
questions.explanation: A long right whisker indicates the upper 25% of data is spread over a wider range, creating a tail to the right (positive skew) (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: If a data set is perfectly symmetric, what is the expected relationship between mean and median?
questions.explanation: In a symmetric distribution, the center of gravity (mean) and middle value (median) coincide. They differ in skewed distributions (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: The highest value in a data set is removed. Which measure is guaranteed to change?
questions.explanation: Range = Max - Min. Removing the maximum definitely changes the Max, thus changing the Range. Median, Mode, and IQR may remain unchanged (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: A cumulative frequency curve is flatter in the middle section. What does this suggest?
options: Data is clustered around the median
Data is spread out around the median
questions.explanation: A flat gradient means a large range of values is needed to accumulate frequency, indicating data is spread out (less consistent) in that region (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: If every value in a data set is decreased by 10, how does the variance change?
questions.explanation: Variance (and SD) measures spread. Shifting all data by a constant (translation) does not change distances between values, so spread measures remain unchanged (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: A data set has Q1 = 15, Median = 25, Q3 = 40. What is the interquartile range?
On a cumulative frequency curve, the lower quartile is found at what percentage of total frequency?
questions.explanation: The lower quartile (Q1) is the 25th percentile, found at 25% of the total cumulative frequency (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: A teacher corrects an error: one score was recorded as 20 instead of 80. How does this affect the mean?
questions.explanation: Correcting 20 to 80 increases the sum of scores. Since Mean = Sum/n, increasing the sum increases the mean (Syllabus 20a).

questions.question: Which statement about standard deviation is correct?
options: SD is always zero or positive
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is calculated using squared distances, so it is always non-negative (≥ 0). It equals zero only when all values are identical (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: Two classes have identical means. Class X has IQR = 8, Class Y has IQR = 20. Which class has more consistent scores in the middle 50%?
questions.explanation: A smaller IQR indicates the middle 50% of scores are more tightly clustered. Class X (IQR=8) has more consistent middle scores (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: A cumulative frequency curve for Class A lies entirely to the right of Class B's curve. What does this indicate?
options: Class A has higher scores overall
Class A has lower scores overall
questions.explanation: If Curve A is to the right of Curve B, for any given cumulative frequency percentage, Class A has a higher corresponding value. This indicates Class A generally has higher scores (Syllabus 20c).
